reason: The finding holds, and nothing in the rules or the data refutes it. (1) The 00:46Z time came from R18-A7 spacing against exp86c, a non-CI file (CONTEXT 12:17Z). R18-A7's stated reason is that two non-CI K2 files co-complete (43/44). The 12:23Z/12:25Z risk-stack line kept 00:46Z for both branches. In branch A, however, exp89r and exp75 are both CI, so the rule has no second non-CI file to act on. (2) Running at the same time costs nothing in the data. On 28 Sep, exp78b (non-CI) and exp79a (CI) were submitted 24 s apart and read at 07:32Z and 09:33Z, with normal L. The three concurrent 26 Sep 21:15-21:38Z files all took about 7 h. (3) The gain arithmetic checks out. Over 14 reads, non-CI L_hi is 6.87-7.81 h, and first-seen already includes the poll quantisation. So 00:46Z reads by about 08:35Z, just 5 min before A-M1's latest 08:40Z header. A '?'/UNUSED needs L_hi > ~7.9 h, a poll gap or a standby. I put that at ~3-8% (the claim says 5-10%). At 00:07Z, exp89p reads 07:00-07:56Z. (4) Two gains the finding misses: (a) At 00:46Z, exp89p's tail comes within ~25-30 min of the earliest CI completions (exp75 >= ~09:04Z, exp89r ~09:0xZ). At 00:07Z the gap is >= ~65 min, so the '0u' UP attribution gets a cleaner separate poll window. (b) Round 27 plancheck found that battery or lid standby cuts the network and the crons. Sending all three branch-A files in one 00:04-00:07Z batch removes a second unattended action 40 min later. (5) Value/private: the file and its hidden run are identical, so there is no lab or node-count artefact and it is not a closed line. This is a pure schedule change. (6) Costs are negligible. The only lost option is an E10 copy displacing exp89p between 00:07 and 00:46Z; E10 would then take a morning slot, which the table often leaves UNUSED. Branch B is unchanged. There is one caveat: the user confirmed '00:46 UTC' by name. The time was derived from the spacing rule, not chosen by the user, but the change should be logged before scoring in the freeze line and told to the user before the night, not only in the morning message.
fix: Adopt as written in the 23:30Z freeze line, logged before scoring. In branch A (exp89r submitted at 00:05Z), send exp89p at 00:07Z in the same night batch, right after exp75. Branch B stays at max(00:46Z, exp89q's actual submit + 40 min). The fallback is unchanged: exp83c takes exp89p's slot only if exp89p has a hard failure. Add one sentence to the pre-freeze message to the user (MSK: 'в ветке A exp89p уйдёт в 03:07 МСК вместо 03:46, тот же файл; причина: единственный не-CI файл ночи, решение по утреннему M1 на ~40 мин раньше'). Keep 00:46Z if the user objects. In the batch log, record that exp89p's read window is 07:00-07:56Z.
realistic_gain: There is no LB or private-score change, since the file is the same. The schedule gains are these. P(A-M1 decision lost to '?') falls from ~3-8% to ~0%, but that matters only when exp89p reads '+'/'0u' (~25-35%). So it saves the exp89l slot in ~1-2% of worlds. exp89l's submit and read also move ~40 min earlier, which adds margin to the 19:30Z card for a CI tail. Separately, UP attribution against the CI completions gets a cleaner poll window, and one fewer unattended night action is exposed to the laptop standby or network risk. The cost is 0 GPU, 0 slots and 0 rules broken.
